name: Alotau
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Alotau geo tag (town centre; a town, not an attraction)
note: Town: provincial capital and gateway to Milne Bay on a natural harbour, with a waterfront, a produce and seafood market, the Turnbull WWII memorial park and the dive trade. The annual Kenu and Kundu Festival is an event, so it is not a spot (mentioned here only).

name: Turnbull War Memorial Park
coordinates_source: OSM historic=monument "Battle for Milne Bay Memorial" (node 2574724137); Wikipedia coords are the naval base, not the park
note: Memorial park: the Milne Bay Memorial to the 1942 Battle of Milne Bay in Alotau (WWII), named by the PNG tourism authority as a Milne Bay war memorial to visit.

name: Vivigani Airfield
note: WWII historic site: Vivigani airfield on Goodenough Island, one of the Battle of Milne Bay airfields; the PNG tourism authority names airfields and bunkers among the battle remnants to see, but no visitor facilities are sourced.

name: No. 2 Strip Milne Bay
coordinates_source: no pin: Wikipedia coords are a sea point (geo type waterbody); owner to supply
note: WWII historic site: No. 2 Strip, the wartime airstrip at Milne Bay built during the 1942 battle; named only generically by the PNG tourism authority (battle airfields), no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Samarai
note: Island: former colonial capital and trading port at the entrance to Milne Bay, a 20-minute walk round, with ruins of its boom-town past and a National Historical Heritage Island listing; reached by boat from Alotau.

name: Logea Island
note: Island: volcanic island in the Samarai group, with the Nuli Sapi eco-resort (a dinghy ride from Alotau, five minutes from Samarai); the PNG tourism authority lists Nuli Sapi and its island as a visit.

name: Doini Island
note: Island: privately owned resort island off the southeastern tip of the mainland, about an hour by boat from Alotau, with white beaches, rainforest, a nine-hole golf course and its own airstrip.

name: Tawali
note: Dive site: reef and drop-offs at Tawali on the coast near Alotau, named by the PNG tourism authority as a world-renowned Milne Bay dive site; reached by boat, with the Tawali Leisure and Dive Resort on the bluff above.

name: Deacon's Reef
note: Dive site: coral reef in Milne Bay named by the PNG tourism authority among its world-renowned dive sites (coral gardens and muck diving).

name: Gonubalabala
note: Dive site: Gonubalabala Island waters in Milne Bay, named by the PNG tourism authority as a dive site and a known manta ray location.

name: Wahoo Point
note: Dive site: point in Milne Bay named by the PNG tourism authority among its world-renowned dive sites for coral gardens and marine life.

name: Nuakata Island
note: Island: island in Milne Bay named in Wikivoyage's custom itinerary options (tours from Alotau via Suau, Samarai, Nuakata and Goodenough); no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Suau Coast
note: Coastal district: the Suau coast east of Alotau, named in Wikivoyage's itinerary options as a tour area; no article under this name (no Wikipedia article; OSM has only a Suau Island village point, not used as a district pin).

name: Kwato Island
note: Island: former London Missionary Society mission station island in Milne Bay with the Kwato Mission history; named by Wikipedia only, no visitor source sourced.

name: Trobriand Islands
note: Island group: the Kiriwina Islands, raised coral atolls in the north of Milne Bay known as the Islands of Love, with yam-harvest dancing, village stays, the Kula ring and white beaches; reached by a twice-weekly PNG Air flight from Alotau.

name: Kiriwina
note: Island: the main Trobriand island with the airstrip, the Losuia township, Kiriwina and Butia lodges, and the village dancing and yam culture the Trobriands are known for.

name: Kitava
note: Island: a Trobriand Islands atoll that is a regular stop for tourist vessels, with coral reefs and the wreck of the Admiral Wiley (1940); named by Wikivoyage and Wikipedia only.

name: Kaileuna
note: Island: one of the major Trobriand Islands, surrounded by coral reefs; named by Wikivoyage as a major island, with no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Vakuta
note: Island: one of the major Trobriand Islands, near the Kiriwina group; named by Wikivoyage as a major island, with no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Louisiade Archipelago
note: Archipelago: about 100 islands in the far southeast of Milne Bay, a diver's paradise and yachting destination with coral reefs; few visitors and reached mainly by private yacht, so a region rather than a single stop.

name: Misima Island
note: Island: the most populated and most accessible Louisiade island, served by air to Bwagaoia with a guest house; a closed gold mine and island-hopping stop named by the PNG tourism authority.

name: Vanatinai Island
coordinates_source: OSM place=island relation "Tagula Island" (7383579), centroid; Vanatinai/Sudest/Tagula are one island
note: Island: reef-fringed volcanic island in the southeast Louisiade, also called Sudest or Tagula; named in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list, with endemic birds and a reef harbour, no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Rossel Island
note: Island: large Louisiade island with a 40 km lagoon inside a fringing reef; named in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list, with historic wrecks on its reefs and no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Deboyne Islands
note: Island group: atoll of reefs and islands in the north Louisiade, with a small ecotourist resort at Nivani that yachtsmen and divers use; named in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list.

name: Calvados Chain
note: Island group: chain of high islands and low coral islands and reefs in the Louisiade; named in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list, no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Duchateau Islands
note: Island group: small islands on the southwestern edge of the Vanatinai barrier reef in the Louisiade; named in Wikivoyage's Louisiade island list.

name: Panapompom Islands
note: Island group: islands of the Panapompom community in the Deboyne group, with the Nivani ecotourist resort project; named by Wikipedia only.

name: Conflict Group
note: Atoll: Conflict Group atoll, with Panasesa Island holding a small eco resort; named by Wikipedia only.

name: Goodenough Island
note: Island: volcanic island of the D'Entrecasteaux group with rainforest, waterfalls, Mount Vineuo and good birdwatching; named as an unspoilt island to explore and a tour destination from Alotau.

name: Mount Vineuo
note: Peak: 2,566 m highest peak of the D'Entrecasteaux Islands on Goodenough Island, named in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay guide; no trail or access details are sourced yet.

name: Normanby Island
note: Island: unspoilt D'Entrecasteaux island with trekking trails, rainforest waterfalls and birdwatching (including the Goldie's bird-of-paradise), with very limited accommodation.

name: Fergusson Island
note: Island: geothermal volcanic island reached only by boat, with trekking trails and birdwatching for a rare bird-of-paradise and the Curl-crested Manucode; its hot springs at Deidei are listed separately.

name: Deidei Hot Springs
note: Hot springs: the active hot springs at Deidei on Fergusson Island, named in Wikipedia's D'Entrecasteaux article; no article or visitor facilities sourced.

name: Woodlark Island
note: Island group: remote Woodlarks to the north of the province, known for wood carvings and coral reefs, listed as an other destination in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay guide.

name: Dobu Island
note: Island: small extinct volcano in the D'Entrecasteaux group, studied by anthropologists; named in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay description and Wikipedia, with no visitor facilities sourced.

name: Sanaroa Island
note: Island: small island of the D'Entrecasteaux group with some of the best coral cover in the Coral Triangle; named in Wikivoyage's Milne Bay description and Wikipedia.
